messages.content: انا اخطط لرحلة لمدينة نيويورك.. كم ستكون درجة الحرارة الاسبوع القادم هناك؟

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.reasoning:
The user asks: "أنا أخطط لرحلة لمدينة نيويورك.. كم ستكون درجة الحرارة الأسبوع القادم هناك؟" They want the temperature forecast for next week in New York City. We need to use the Open-Meteo API via the provided function. We need to get the forecast for next week. The function signature: requests_get with params: latitude, longitude, elevation optional. We need to specify the URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint. The Open-Meteo API endpoint for forecast is something like "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast". We need to provide query parameters: latitude, longitude. For NYC, approximate coordinates: latitude 40.7128, longitude -74.0060. We also need to specify the forecast parameters: we want daily temperature. The Open-Meteo API supports daily parameters like "temperature_2m_max" and "temperature_2m_min". We can request daily max and min temperatures. Also we need to set "start_date" and "end_date" for next week. Let's compute dates: Today is 2026-10-20. Next week: from 2026-10-27 to 2026-11-02? Actually "next week" could mean the upcoming week starting Monday after this week. But we can interpret as the next 7 days from today. So start_date = 2026-10-21, end_date = 2026-10-27. Or maybe they want the next week after this week: from 2026-10-24 to 2026-10-30. But let's choose next 7 days: 2026-10-21 to 2026-10-27. We'll request daily max and min temperatures. The API requires "daily=temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min". Also "timezone=America/New_York" to get local times. So the function call:

{
  url: "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast",
  params: {
    latitude: 40.7128,
    longitude: -74.0060,
    daily: "temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min",
    start_date: "2026-10-21",
    end_date: "2026-10-27",
    timezone: "America/New_York"
  }
}

We don't need headers. The function will return JSON. Then we parse the JSON to extract daily temperatures. Then we respond with the forecast.

We need to call the function.
